page: Amazon Web Services m9g.48xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the arm64 architecture, the instance features 192 dedicated physical cores utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 model running at 3.3 GHz. It is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 96 MB of L3 cache. This instance operates on the Nitro hypervisor and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps, though it does not include local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core performance scoring 381,353.24 and PassMark CPU score reaching 107,221.26, both placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is also in the top tier, registering 27,574.84 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 729.22 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The instance demonstrates strong database and web serving capabilities, achieving 507.16 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 359.97 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core scoring 2,008.79, placing it in the middle 50%. Additionally, LLM text generation for a small 135M model is slow at 21.54 tokens/sec, representing a performance tradeoff for sequential text generation tasks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m9g.48xlarge leverages the ARMv9 architecture to deliver high resource density and multi-threaded throughput without the premium associated with traditional x86 architectures. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs reduces overhead for workloads that rely on network-attached storage or do not require hardware acceleration. This profile is suitable for large-scale multi-threaded applications, high-throughput database operations, static web serving, and multi-threaded decompression tasks.
